**Read this first — deviations and data-path notes**

- **No watchlist exists in this sandbox.** `research/watchlist.yaml` (skill Step 1/Step 4) is absent — same condition as the sibling pre-market cron.
- The skill's *Watchlist EOD review* section is therefore **omitted rather than fabricated**; no default watchlist was created. This is a missing-input condition, not a data failure.
- **The MCP finance tier does not exist in this Cloud session.** The catalog holds 15 tools across two providers (`matrix`, `email_workbench_credentials`), `partial=false`,
- no provider failures, and a keyword search for yahoo/tradingview/stock/screener returned **0 hits**.
- No MCP finance call was ever attempted, so there are **zero MCP call failures**; the run executed on the public-HTTP stack (one fallback, terminated there).
- **Fire time is ~6 hours late relative to the intended slot.** The upside:
- the after-hours session (ends 20:00 ET) is complete, so every after-hours print below is a *final* 20:00 ET mark, not a snapshot.
- The downside: this brief is published long after the tape it describes.
- **TradingView's `change` column carried a stale reference on 1 of 44 cross-checked names** (MSGK, apparent +40.18% vs Yahoo +5.54%).
- All published percentage changes use Yahoo's `regularMarketChangePercent`; TV supplied the universe, the closes and the after-hours prints.
- **CNBC's `last` is the last *trade*, not the official close** (MSGK: CNBC $289.39 "UNCH" vs official close $305.42).
- Official closes are taken from Yahoo; CNBC is used for identity, market cap, relative volume and the timestamped after-hours print.
- **Cboe's put/call markup carries no date stamp.** The page was fetched at 22:45 ET, so the session is *inferred* as 2026-10-27 (Cboe publishes at 20:00 ET).
- Treat the ratio as a same-session figure with an inferred date, not a stamped one.
- **One apparent cross-source conflict was left standing rather than smoothed:** the Nikkei. Reuters' Oct 27 Tokyo close was **+1.7%**; Yahoo's `^N225` at 22:19 ET reads **+1.07%** —
- but that is the *live Oct 28 Tokyo session*, a different session, not a disagreement about the same close. Both are labelled where used.
- **A multi-hour "second read" was not possible on the after-hours tape** (the session is closed), so the AH spread is evidenced by an independent third source instead (see §6).

**TL;DR**

- A **narrow, AI-led risk-on day with a violent single-name tail**. The Nasdaq Composite gained **+1.18%** to 26,477.81 — its best session in nearly a month —
- while the **Dow was flat at +0.03%**, and the S&P 500 added **+0.60%** to 7,722.60.
- Breadth was genuinely broad (**58.4%** of 5,716 US listings advanced, median **+0.32%**), and the move was **one-sided at the tails**:
- 717 names rose ≥5% versus 216 that fell ≥5%, and in large caps the skew was **225 up vs 41 down**.
- The engine was semiconductors (SOX **+3.6%**), the continuation of the AI-optimism trade after Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO filing, Nvidia's commitment to invest in Meta's equity offering, and CLS's EMS commentary;
- small caps did not lag (Russell 2000 **+1.16%**). Volatility collapsed — **VIX −4.73% to 17.52**, VXN −5.64% — and Cboe equity put/call printed **0.59**.

- Two things broke the surface. **Boeing fell 10.69% to $168.18** on a Q3 miss *and* a production slippage confession, which is most of the reason the Dow went nowhere.
- And the **refining complex was gutted** (VLO −9.24%, MPC −7.36%, PSX −7.03%, DK −10.41%, PARR −10.39%, PBF −8.59%, DINO −8.81%, CVI −7.40%) —
- the worst refining session since April 2025 — on a **crack-spread repricing, not an oil story**:
- WTI settled only −1.83% to $99.90 while refiners fell three to five times harder than the products they sell, as Iran de-escalation talk and a Russian-diesel waiver compressed the distillate-risk premium.

- After the bell, the tape split hard:
- **Manhattan Associates +10.27%**, **ICON +9.85%**, **Ultra Clean +9.75%** and **DMC Global +16.45%** against **Rapport Therapeutics −20.04%**, **Intapp −16.67%**, **Enphase −15.49%**, **Beta Bionics −10.38%**, **CoStar −8.15%**, **Robinhood −7.63%**, **NXP −7.31%** and **Seagate −5.52%** —
- the last two despite beating and raising. **Tomorrow is the FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET, Chair Warsh at 2:30 PM ET) with Microsoft and Alphabet reporting after the close.**

Also: **INTA −8.91%, DINO −8.81%, PBF −8.59%, AIT −8.35%, GWRE −8.05%, EEFT −7.72%, CVI −7.40%, MPC −7.36%, PSX −7.03%**.

- **The Boeing read.** The loss narrowed to $116mn (26c/share; adjusted −34c) and free cash flow rose to $464mn, and backlog hit a record **$745bn** —
- but revenue of $24.19bn missed, adjusted EPS missed by 14–69% depending on the consensus used, commercial-airplanes margin went to **−6.5%**, and CEO Kelly Ortberg said the 737 Max rate stays at 47/month with **52/month not until 2H 2027**, meaning the 500-jet 2026 target is missed.
- A supply-chain dispute with supplier Vaero over a wing component is in the background.
- Shares closed at their **lowest since April 2025**, down more than 22% year-to-date — the second-worst DJIA performer — on volume roughly **7× the 10-day average**.
- The market punished the *schedule*, not the quarter.

- **The refiner read — why refiners fell 3–5× harder than oil.** WTI settled **−1.83% to $99.90** and Brent −1.67% to $113.88; gasoline futures lost 2.2% and heating oil 2.7%.
- Refiners fell three to five times that. The margin story, not the barrel: the **3-2-1 crack spread has compressed to roughly $50/bbl from over $72 a month earlier**;
- Iran de-escalation talk (Khamenei and his security chief discussing conditions to end the conflict) removed part of the geopolitical risk premium that had made the trade work;
- the **Trump-backed Russian diesel waiver** threatened the distillate tightness that produced Valero's record $39.24/bbl Q3 margin; **Freedom Broker downgraded VLO to Sell (target $358)** against a Wells Fargo $489;
- **Michael Burry** flagged Valero as a stretched holding he may trim; and **BTIG** warned of a correction after the refining index's ~124% year-to-date gain.
- Marathon ended a **10-month winning streak** (the record run since 2012–13).
- Note the irony: Valero's Q3 was a blowout (adjusted EPS $23.89 vs ~$21.28 consensus, revenue $46.1bn) and the stock still fell 9.24% to its worst day since April 2025.
